227.stem:
Tina inherits $\text{\textdollar}60\,000$ and invests it in an account earning interest at a rate of $0.5\%$ per month. Each month, immediately after the interest has been paid, Tina withdraws $\text{\textdollar}800$.

The amount in the account immediately after the $n$th withdrawal can be determined using the recurrence relation

$$A_n=A_{n-1}(1.005)-800,$$

where $n=1,2,3,\ldots$ and $A_0=60\,000$.

parts.latex: Use the recurrence relation to find the amount of money in the account immediately after the third withdrawal.
Calculate the amount of interest earned in the first three months.
Calculate the amount of money in the account immediately after the 94th withdrawal.

criteria: Finds the value of $A_1$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Total withdrawals after 3 months:
$$\begin{aligned} &= 800\times 3 \\ &= \$2400 \end{aligned}$$
Balance is reduced by:
$$\begin{aligned} &= 60\,000 - 58\,492.49 \\ &= \$1507.51 \end{aligned}$$
Interest:
$$\begin{aligned} &= \$2400 - \$1507.51 \\ &= \$892.49 \end{aligned}$$
$\therefore$ the interest earned is $\$892.49$.
criteria: Finds by how much the balance is reduced, or equivalent merit
Finds an expression for $A_{94}$, or equivalent merit
Attempts to develop a formula for $A_{94}$, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
On the day that Megan was born, her grandfather deposited $\text{\textdollar}5000$ into an account earning 3% per annum compounded annually. On each birthday after this, her grandfather deposited $\text{\textdollar}1000$ into the same account, making his final deposit on Megan's 17th birthday. That is, a total of 18 deposits were made.

Let $A_n$ be the amount in the account on Megan's $n$th birthday, after the deposit is made.

Show that $A_3=\text{\textdollar}8554.54$.

On her 17th birthday, just after the final deposit is made, Megan has $\text{\textdollar}30\,025.83$ in her account. You are NOT required to show this.

Megan then decides to leave all the money in the same account continuing to earn interest at 3% per annum compounded annually. On her 18th birthday, and on each birthday after this, Megan withdraws $\text{\textdollar}2000$ from the account.

How many withdrawals of $\text{\textdollar}2000$ will Megan be able to make?

criteria: Finds the correct value of $A_1$, or equivalent merit
Finds the correct expression for the amount after $n$ withdrawals using the sum of GP formula, or equivalent merit
Attempts to find an expression for the amount after $n$ withdrawals, or equivalent merit

194.stem:
On the first day of November, Jia deposits \$10 000 into a new account which earns 0.4% interest per month, compounded monthly. At the end of each month, after the interest is added to the account, Jia intends to withdraw \$$M$ from the account.

Let $A_n$ be the amount (in dollars) in Jia's account at the end of $n$ months.

parts.latex:

292.stem:
Maroun deposits \$500 000 into a retirement fund which earns compound interest at the rate of 0.3% per month.

Maroun withdraws spending money from the retirement fund at the end of each month.

The incomplete table below shows the account activity for the first four months and the balance at the end of the fifth month.

\exfigure{510_q28_1}

figures.cap: incomplete retirement fund table (crossed out by hand)

parts.latex: Calculate the amount of money that Maroun withdrew at the end of the fifth month.

Maroun is going to withdraw \$7500 at the end of each month, starting from the end of the sixth month.

The recurrence relation $A_n=A_{n-1}\times 1.003-7500$ models this situation, where $A_n$ is the balance in the retirement fund at the end of the $n$th month.

Determine the balance in Maroun's retirement fund at the end of the seventh month.

Maroun is offered an alternative retirement fund, where interest is paid at 3.2% per annum, compounded daily.

By calculating the effective annual rate of interest for both retirement funds, or otherwise, determine whether Maroun should remain with the current retirement fund or change to the alternative retirement fund.

solutions.latex:
Balance at the end of the fourth month:
$$496994.00+1490.98-3800=494684.98$$

$\therefore$ Balance at the end of the fourth month is $\$494\,684.98$.

Interest earned at the end of the fifth month:
$$494684.98\times 0.003=1484.05$$

$\therefore$ Interest earned at the end of the fifth month is $\$1484.05$.

Amount Maroun withdrew at the end of the fifth month:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Balance} &= P+I-M \\ M &= P+I-\text{Balance} \\ &= 494684.98+1484.05-491969.03 \\ &= 4200 \end{aligned}$$

$\therefore$ Maroun withdrew $\$4200$ at the end of the fifth month.
criteria: Finds the interest earned at the end of the fifth month, or equivalent merit
Finds the balance at the end of the fourth month, or equivalent merit
Determines the balance at the end of the sixth month, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Effective annual rate of interest for the current retirement fund:
$$\begin{aligned} (1+0.003)^{12}-1 &= 0.036599\ldots \\ &\approx 3.66\%\text{ p.a.} \end{aligned}$$

Effective annual rate of interest for the alternative retirement fund:
$$\begin{aligned} \left(1+\dfrac{0.032}{365}\right)^{365}-1 &= 0.032516\ldots \\ &\approx 3.25\%\text{ p.a.} \end{aligned}$$

The effective annual rate of interest for the alternative retirement fund is less than Maroun's current retirement fund, hence Maroun should stay with his current retirement fund.

Alternatively, compare the future value (FV) of one dollar invested in both funds.

Current fund:
$$\text{FV}=(1+0.3\%)^{12}=\$1.03659998$$

Alternative fund:
$$\text{FV}=\left(1+\dfrac{3.2\%}{365}\right)^{365}=\$1.032516057$$

The FV of the alternative fund is less than the FV of the current fund, hence Maroun should stay with his current retirement fund.
criteria: Finds the effective annual rate of interest for one of the funds, or equivalent merit

489.stem: Jack intends to deposit \$80 into a savings account on the first day of each month for 24 months. The interest rate during this time is 6\% per annum, compounded monthly.

figures.cap: partial table of future value interest factors with entry A

parts.latex: Calculate how much money Jack will have in his account at the end of the 24 months.

A table of future value interest factors could have been used to calculate how much money Jack would have in his account at the end of the 24 months.

Part of the table is shown.

\exfigure{1628_q24_1}

What is the value of $A$ in the table? Give your answer correct to 3 decimal places.
parts.note: Annuity interest-factor table look-up: Standard (2024 Advanced annuities use the GP formula only) · Standard: MST-12-S2-03

solutions.latex:
The monthly rate is $\dfrac{6\%}{12}=0.5\%$, so each month the balance is multiplied by $1.005$.

The first deposit accrues interest for 24 months.

$\therefore$ Its future value is $80(1.005)^{24}$.

The next deposit accrues interest for 23 months, and so on, down to 1 month for the last deposit.

Summing the geometric series ($a=1.005$, $r=1.005$, 24 terms):
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total} &= 80(1.005)^{24}+80(1.005)^{23}+\cdots+80(1.005)^{1}\\ &= 80\left[(1.005)^1+(1.005)^2+\cdots+(1.005)^{24}\right]\\ &= 80\times(1.005)\left[\dfrac{(1.005)^{24}-1}{1.005-1}\right]\\ &= 2044.73\end{aligned}$$
$\therefore$ Jack will have $\$2044.73$.
criteria: Sets up an appropriate series, or equivalent merit
Finds a correct term in the series, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The future value of an annuity of \$1 for 24 periods is $A$, so the future value of \$80 per period is $80A$.
$$\begin{aligned} 80A &= 2044.73\\ A &= \dfrac{2044.73}{80}\\ &= 25.559\end{aligned}$$

parts.latex:
Ali decides to invest \$500 at the end of each month into an annuity. The interest rate quoted is 9\% per annum, compounded monthly.

Let $A_n$ represent the future value of the annuity after $n$ months.

Which recurrence relation models this financial situation?

solutions.latex:
The monthly interest rate is
$$\dfrac{9\%}{12}=0.75\%$$
so each month the balance is multiplied by $1.0075$, then the \$500 deposit at the end of the month is added.

Nothing is invested initially, so $A_0=0$.
$$A_n=A_{n-1}\times1.0075+500,\quad A_0=0$$

parts.latex:
Mr. Fredricksen has just retired from work as a balloon salesman. He has received a superannuation payment and has worked out that he will require \$7000 per month for the next 20 years.

Mr. Fredricksen intends to invest a set amount ($P$) at 6% p.a. interest compounding monthly and withdraws \$7000 from this account at the end of each month.
Show that the amount $A_3$ remaining in the account after the third withdrawal of \$7000 is $A_3=P(1.005)^3-7000\left[(1.005)^2+1.005+1\right]$
Find the amount $P$ that will need to be invested if he is to withdraw \$7000 each month for the next 20 years. Express your answer to the nearest cent.

criteria: Sums the geometric series, or equivalent merit

meta.corrected: Corrected from source: the GP sum denominator was written $1.005$; it is $1.005-1=0.005$ (the next line, $1400000$, and the answer are unchanged).

parts.latex: An amount of \$6000 is invested at an interest rate of 6.5% p.a. compounded annually. How much interest, to the nearest dollar, has been earned after 15 years?

solutions.latex:
Compound interest formula:
$$\begin{aligned} A &= P(1+r)^n \\ &= 6000(1.065)^{15} \\ &= 15431.0\ldots \end{aligned}$$
Interest earned:
$$\begin{aligned} I &= A-P \\ &= 15431.0\ldots-6000 \\ &= 9431.0\ldots \\ &\approx \$9431 \end{aligned}$$

parts.latex: Use the future value table above to find Hannah’s account balance at the end of December 2023.

parts.latex: At the beginning of January 2024, Hannah starts working at a new job and decides to increase her monthly investments to \$200. If Hannah continues this for the year, show that her account balance at the end of December 2024 is \$3776.76.
parts.note: Annuity future value from an interest-factor table look-up (plus compound growth of the earlier balance); 2024 Advanced annuities use the GP formula only · Standard: MST-12-S2-03

parts.latex:
At the beginning of January 2025, Hannah starts her trip and stops contributing to the account. Instead, she withdraws \$400 from the account \textbf{at the start} of each month to cover expenses. The account continues to earn interest at 6% p.a. compounded monthly. Show that Hannah’s account balance, $A_n$, at the end of the $n$th month of her trip is given by:

$$A_n=3776.76(1.005)^n-80400(1.005^n-1)$$
How many \$400 withdrawals can Hannah make from her travel fund?

solutions.latex:
$n=1$ year $=12$ months, $r=6\%$ p.a. $=0.5\%$ per month, so the factor is $12.3356$.
$$\begin{aligned} FV &= M\times\text{factor} \\ &= 100\times 12.3356 \\ &= 1233.56 \end{aligned}$$
$\therefore$ Hannah has \$1233.56.

The 2023 balance grows for 12 months at $0.5\%$ per month, plus the new annuity ($n=12$, $r=0.5\%$):
$$\begin{aligned} FV &= FV_{\text{lump}}+FV_{\text{instal}} \\ &= P(1+r)^n+M\times\text{factor} \\ &= 1233.56(1+0.5\%)^{12}+200\times 12.3356 \\ &= 3776.763\ldots \\ &\approx 3776.76 \end{aligned}$$
$\therefore$ Hannah has \$3776.76.

criteria: Writes $A_n$ with the geometric series $400(1.005+\cdots+1.005^n)$, or equivalent merit
Correct expressions for $A_2$ and $A_3$ ($A_1$ not required), or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The fund runs out when $A_n=0$:
$$\begin{aligned} 0 &= 3776.76(1.005)^n-80400(1.005)^n+80400 \\ &= -76623.24(1.005)^n+80400 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} 76623.24(1.005)^n &= 80400 \\ (1.005)^n &= 1.049\ldots \\ n\ln 1.005 &= \ln 1.049\ldots \\ n &= 9.64\ldots \end{aligned}$$
$\therefore$ Hannah can make 9 withdrawals.
criteria: Sets $A_n=0$ and simplifies to $-76623.24(1.005)^n+80400=0$, or equivalent merit

meta.marker_note: The answer must be rounded down (9 withdrawals).

parts.latex: What amount to the nearest dollar must be invested now at 6% per annum, compounded monthly, so that in four years time it will have grown to \$50,000?

solutions.latex:
The monthly rate is $\dfrac{0.06}{12}=0.005$ and there are $n=4\times12=48$ months.

Using $A=P(1+r)^n$:
$$\begin{aligned}P(1.005)^{48}&=50000\\P&=\dfrac{50000}{1.005^{48}}\\&\approx\$39\,355\end{aligned}$$

1269.stem:
When Fred was born, his parents opened a new savings account and made a deposit of \$300. At the start of each subsequent six-month period, his parents make a deposit of \$300. The account earns an interest rate of 6% per annum, compounded half-yearly.

Let $A_n$ be the amount (in dollars) in the account at the end of $n^{th}$ half-year.

parts.latex: Show that the amount available for withdrawal at the end of the 18$^{\text{th}}$ year will be \$19552 to the nearest dollar. (Assume that no withdrawals are made from the fund during this time.)

solutions.latex:
$r=\dfrac{6\%}{2}=3\%$ per half-year.

Each deposit is made at the start of a half-year and earns interest for that half-year:
$$\begin{aligned}A_1&=300(1.03)\\A_2&=(A_1+300)\times1.03\\&=(300\times1.03+300)\times1.03\\&=300\times1.03^2+300\times1.03\end{aligned}$$

Continuing the pattern, the bracket is a GP with $a=1.03$, $r=1.03$ and $n$ terms, summed with $S_n=\dfrac{a(r^n-1)}{r-1}$:
$$\begin{aligned}A_1&=300(1.03)\\A_2&=300\times1.03^2+300\times1.03\\&\;\;\vdots\\A_n&=300\times1.03^n+300\times1.03^{n-1}+\dots+300\times1.03\\&=300(1.03^n+1.03^{n-1}+\dots+1.03)\\&=300\times1.03\times\dfrac{1.03^n-1}{1.03-1}\\&=10300(1.03^n-1)\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Writes an expression for $A_n$, or uses the sum of a GP formula without establishing $A_n$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
$18$ years $=36$ half-years, so $n=36$:
$$\begin{aligned}A_{36}&=10300(1.03^{36}-1)\\&=\$19\,552\text{ (nearest dollar)}\end{aligned}$$

1672.stem: Melinda visits a bank and makes a single deposit of \$$Q$. The annual interest rate is 3.5%.

parts.latex:
Melinda wishes to withdraw \$8000 at the end of each year for a period of $n$ years. Show that an expression for the minimum value of $Q$ is

$$\dfrac{8000}{1.035}+\dfrac{8000}{1.035^2}+\dfrac{8000}{1.035^3}+\cdots+\dfrac{8000}{1.035^n}$$
Hence, or otherwise, find the minimum value $Q$ that would permit Melinda to withdraw annual amounts of \$8000 indefinitely. Give your answer to the nearest dollar.

solutions.latex:
Let $A_n$ be the balance after the $n$th withdrawal. Each year the balance is multiplied by $1.035$, then $\$8000$ is withdrawn:
$$\begin{aligned} A_1&=Q\times1.035-8000 \\ A_2&=A_1\times1.035-8000 \\ &=\left(Q\times1.035-8000\right)1.035-8000 \\ &=Q\times1.035^2-8000\times1.035-8000 \\ A_3&=A_2\times1.035-8000 \\ &=Q\times1.035^3-8000\times1.035^2-8000\times1.035-8000 \\ &=Q\times1.035^3-8000\left(1.035^2+1.035+1\right) \end{aligned}$$
Continuing the pattern,
$$A_n=Q\times1.035^n-8000\left(1+1.035+\cdots+1.035^{n-1}\right)$$
The minimum value of $Q$ leaves nothing after $n$ withdrawals, $A_n=0$:
$$\begin{aligned} Q\times1.035^n&=8000\left(1+1.035+1.035^2+1.035^3+\cdots+1.035^{n-1}\right) \\ Q&=\dfrac{8000}{1.035^n}+\dfrac{8000}{1.035^{n-1}}+\dfrac{8000}{1.035^{n-2}}+\cdots+\dfrac{8000}{1.035} \\ &=\dfrac{8000}{1.035}+\dfrac{8000}{1.035^2}+\cdots+\dfrac{8000}{1.035^n} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the correct expression for $A_n$, or equivalent merit
Writes the correct expression for $A_1$, $A_2$ or $A_3$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The expression in part (a) is a geometric series with
$$\begin{aligned} a&=\dfrac{8000}{1.035} \\ r&=\dfrac{1}{1.035} \end{aligned}$$
Withdrawing indefinitely means $n\to\infty$, so the minimum value is the limiting sum (as $|r|<1$):
$$\begin{aligned} Q&=\dfrac{a}{1-r} \\ &=\dfrac{\frac{8000}{1.035}}{1-\frac{1}{1.035}} \\ &=\$228\,571.43 \\ &\approx\$228\,571 \text{ (nearest dollar)} \end{aligned}$$
Alternative solution: the yearly interest must cover the withdrawal, so
$$\begin{aligned} Q\times3.5\%&=8000 \\ Q&=\dfrac{8000}{3.5\%} \\ &=\$228\,571.43 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Uses the correct limiting sum expression to find the minimum value, or equivalent merit

meta.corrected: Corrected from source: the question asks for the nearest dollar, so the answer is $\$228\,571$; the guideline stopped at $\$228\,571.43$.

parts.latex: An investment of \$4000 earns interest at a rate of $r\%$ p.a. over a period of one year. How much more interest would the investment earn, if interest is compounded half-yearly rather than yearly? Find the answer in terms of $r$.

solutions.latex:
With yearly compounding at $\dfrac{r}{100}$:
$$A_1=4000\left(1+\dfrac{r}{100}\right)$$
With half-yearly compounding the rate per half-year is $\dfrac{r}{200}$, for $2$ periods:
$$\begin{aligned} A_2 &= 4000\left(1+\dfrac{r}{200}\right)^2 \\ &= 4000\left(1+\dfrac{r}{100}+\dfrac{r^2}{40000}\right) \end{aligned}$$
The extra interest is
$$\begin{aligned} A_2-A_1 &= 4000\left(1+\dfrac{r}{100}+\dfrac{r^2}{40000}\right)-4000\left(1+\dfrac{r}{100}\right) \\ &= 4000\cdot\dfrac{r^2}{40000} \\ &= \dfrac{r^2}{10} \end{aligned}$$
So the investment earns $\$\dfrac{r^2}{10}$ more.

1807.stem:
Preeti deposits \$300 into a savings account on 1 January 2024. The account accrues interest at the rate of $3.6\%$ p.a. compounding monthly. Preeti plans to deposit \$300 at the start of every month thereafter until the end of 2029.

Let $A_n$ be the amount that Preeti has in her account at the end of the $n$th month (where the 1$^{\text{st}}$ month is January 2024).

parts.latex: By first obtaining expressions for $A_1$, $A_2$, and $A_3$, show that $A_n=100300(1.003^n-1)$

Preeti quits her job and goes to university for two years starting in 2028. As a result, she is unable to make any monthly deposits in the years 2028-2029. However, while she is at university, her bank offers her a special interest rate of $6\%$ p.a. compounding monthly.

Calculate the value of Preeti’s account at the end of 2029, and find how much more money she would have had if she hadn’t gone to university.

solutions.latex:
The monthly rate is $\dfrac{3.6\%}{12}=0.3\%=0.003$, so each month's balance is multiplied by $1.003$.

Each deposit of \$300 is made at the start of the month, so it earns interest for that month.
$$\begin{aligned} A_1 &= 300(1.003) \\ A_2 &= \big(A_1+300\big)(1.003) \\ &= 300(1.003^2+1.003) \\ A_3 &= \big(A_2+300\big)(1.003) \\ &= 300(1.003^3+1.003^2+1.003) \end{aligned}$$
Hence
$$A_n=300\left(1.003^n+1.003^{n-1}+\cdots+1.003\right)$$
This is a geometric series with first term $a=300(1.003)$, common ratio $r=1.003$ and $n$ terms.

Using $S_n=\dfrac{a(r^n-1)}{r-1}$:
$$\begin{aligned} A_n &= \dfrac{300(1.003)\left(1.003^n-1\right)}{1.003-1} \\ &= \dfrac{300.9}{0.003}\left(1.003^n-1\right) \\ &= 100300\left(1.003^n-1\right) \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Obtains the expression for $A_n$ as a geometric series, or equivalent merit
Obtains correct expressions for $A_1$, $A_2$ and $A_3$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Deposits are made for $2024$ to $2027$, which is $4\times 12=48$ months. The balance at the end of $2027$ is
$$\begin{aligned} A_{48} &= 100300\left(1.003^{48}-1\right) \\ &\approx \$15\,509.91 \end{aligned}$$
For $2028$ and $2029$ there are no deposits, $24$ months at $\dfrac{6\%}{12}=0.5\%$ per month:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Value at end of 2029} &= 15\,509.91\times 1.005^{24} \\ &\approx \$17\,482.14 \end{aligned}$$
If she had not gone to university, deposits continue for $72$ months at $0.3\%$:
$$\begin{aligned} A_{72} &= 100300\left(1.003^{72}-1\right) \\ &\approx \$24\,142.32 \end{aligned}$$
Difference:
$$24\,142.32-17\,482.14\approx \$6660.18$$
Hence her account is worth about $\$17\,482.14$, and she would have had about $\$6660.18$ more.
criteria: Finds the value at the end of $2029$ and attempts $A_{72}$, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: Jacinta is gifted \$5000 from her grandmother. The money is invested for 18 years, earning 7% p.a. in interest, compounded monthly. Calculate the effective annual interest rate of the investment over the 18 years. Answer as a percentage correct to two decimal places.

solutions.latex:
Method 1: find the final amount, then the annual rate that gives the same growth over $18$ years.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=5000\left(1+\dfrac{0.07}{12}\right)^{12\times 18} \\ &=17\,562.69661\ldots \\ 17\,562.69661&=5000(1+r)^{18} \\ (1+r)^{18}&=3.512539\ldots \\ 1+r&=\sqrt[18]{3.512539}=1.072290081 \\ r&=0.072290 \\ &\approx 7.23\%\text{ (to 2 dp)}\end{aligned}$$
Method 2: the effective annual rate is $\text{EAR}=\left(1+\dfrac{r}{n}\right)^n-1$.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{EAR}&=\left(1+\dfrac{0.07}{12}\right)^{12}-1 \\ &=0.07229\ldots \\ &\approx 7.23\%\text{ (to 2 dp)}\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Substitutes into the compound interest formula, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Sally contributes \$7200 each year into a superannuation fund for the first 15 years of her working life. For the next 20 years until retirement, she decides to increase this, and invest a total of \$10000 each year. Each contribution is paid at the beginning of the year.

If the investment earns 7% per annum paid yearly over whole period, how much will her investment be upon retiring? (Show all your working)

solutions.latex:
Each contribution is paid at the start of the year, so the first contribution earns interest for the whole $15$ years. After $15$ years the amount is a geometric series with first term $7200(1.07)$, common ratio $1.07$ and $15$ terms:
$$\begin{aligned}A_1&=7200(1.07)\\ A_2&=\left(A_1+7200\right)(1.07)=7200(1.07)^2+7200(1.07)\\ &\ \ \vdots\\ A_{15}&=7200(1.07)^{15}+7200(1.07)^{14}+\cdots+7200(1.07)^2+7200(1.07)\\ &=\dfrac{7200(1.07)\left(1.07^{15}-1\right)}{1.07-1}\\ &=193\,593.9855\ldots\end{aligned}$$
From then on the contributions are $\$10\,000$ at the start of each year. The new contributions form a geometric series with first term $10\,000(1.07)$, common ratio $1.07$ and $20$ terms, and $A_{15}$ grows for a further $20$ years:
$$\begin{aligned}A_{16}&=\left(A_{15}+10\,000\right)(1.07)=A_{15}(1.07)+10\,000(1.07)\\ A_{17}&=\left(A_{16}+10\,000\right)(1.07)=A_{15}(1.07)^2+10\,000(1.07)^2+10\,000(1.07)\\ &\ \ \vdots\\ A_{35}&=A_{15}(1.07)^{20}+10\,000(1.07)^{20}+10\,000(1.07)^{19}+\cdots+10\,000(1.07)\\ &=A_{15}(1.07)^{20}+\dfrac{10\,000(1.07)\left(1.07^{20}-1\right)}{1.07-1}\\ &\approx\$1\,187\,799.41\end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{her investment on retiring is }\$1\,187\,799.41\text{ (nearest cent)}$$
criteria: Successively finds $A_{16}$ and $A_{17}$ or an expression for $A_{35}$ with working

parts.latex: Pearl invests \$12000 into a saving account that offers an interest rate of $4.15\%$ p.a. compounded yearly. Gary invests \$12000 into an account with a different interest rate that compounds monthly. What interest rate as a $\%\ p \cdot a.$ does Gary's bank offer if after 4 years both Pearl and Gary have the same amount in their accounts?

solutions.latex:
Pearl's balance after 4 years is
$$12000(1.0415)^4=14119.47$$
Gary's account has monthly compounding for $48$ months at $\dfrac{r}{12}$ per month. For equal balances:
$$\begin{aligned}12000\left(1+\dfrac{r}{12}\right)^{48}&=14119.47\\\left(1+\dfrac{r}{12}\right)^{48}&=(1.0415)^4\\1+\dfrac{r}{12}&=(1.0415)^{\frac{1}{12}}\\r&=12\left[(1.0415)^{\frac{1}{12}}-1\right]\approx 0.0407\end{aligned}$$
So Gary's rate is $4.07\%$ p.a., which is option B.

2323.stem: Eugene deposits a sum of money into a bank account at the start of each year. The bank offers interest of $4\%$ p.a. compounded every 6 months. Let $A_n$ be the value of the account after $n$ years and $P$ be the value of each deposit.

parts.latex:
Show that the total value in the account after 3 years is given by:

$$A_3=P(1.02)^6+P(1.02)^4+P(1.02)^2.$$
Show that $A_n=\dfrac{2601}{101}P\left(1.02^{2n}-1\right)$.
If Eugene saves \$500 000 dollars at the end of 25 years, find the size of his deposits.

solutions.latex:
Interest is $\dfrac{4}{2}=2\%$ per 6 months, so each year the balance is multiplied by $(1.02)^2$. A deposit $P$ is made at the start of each year.
$$\begin{aligned}A_1&=P(1.02)^2\\A_2&=\left(P(1.02)^2+P\right)(1.02)^2\\&=P(1.02)^4+P(1.02)^2\\A_3&=\left(P(1.02)^4+P(1.02)^2+P\right)(1.02)^2\\&=P(1.02)^6+P(1.02)^4+P(1.02)^2\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Writes $A_2$ (or $A_3$) in terms of the previous balance, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Source had no marks breakdown; rubric written by us. Reason for the factor (1.02)^2 added.

solutions.latex:
From part (a), the pattern of the terms continues, with $n$ deposits.
$$\begin{aligned}A_n&=P(1.02)^{2n}+P(1.02)^{2n-2}+\cdots+P(1.02)^2\\&=P(1.02)^2\left[1+1.02^2+1.02^4+\cdots+1.02^{2n-2}\right]\end{aligned}$$
The bracket is a geometric series with $a=1$, $r=1.02^2$ and $n$ terms, so its sum is $\dfrac{r^n-1}{r-1}$.
$$\begin{aligned}A_n&=P(1.02)^2\times\dfrac{\left(1.02^2\right)^n-1}{1.02^2-1}\\&=P\cdot\dfrac{1.0404}{0.0404}\left(1.02^{2n}-1\right)\\&=\dfrac{2601}{101}P\left(1.02^{2n}-1\right)\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Recognises a geometric series with $a=1$, $r=1.02^2$ and $n$ terms, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Source had no marks breakdown; rubric written by us. Source jumped from (1.02)^2/(1.02^2-1) to 2601/101; the step 1.0404/0.0404 = 10404/404 = 2601/101 added.

parts.latex: What amount (to the nearest dollar) must be invested now at $4\%$ per annum, compounded quarterly, so that in five years it will have grown to \$60 000?

solutions.latex:
The quarterly rate is $r=\dfrac{4\%}{4}=0.01$ and the number of quarters is $n=5\times 4=20$.
$$\begin{aligned}60\,000&=P(1.01)^{20}\\P&=\dfrac{60\,000}{1.01^{20}}\\&=49\,172.66\ldots\end{aligned}$$
To the nearest dollar this is $\$49\,173$, option B.

The table below gives the present value interest factors for an annuity of \$1 per period, for various interest, $r$ and numbers of periods, $n$.

parts.latex: Anne plans to invest \$500 each month for 4 years at 4.2% per annum. Use the table to calculate the present value of the annuity.

parts.latex: Calculate the future value of Anne’s investment.

Trevor decides to take out a personal loan of \$49 000 to buy a car. Use the table to determine the total interest paid if the loan is paid in full after 46 months at an interest rate of 0.5% per month.
parts.note: Loan repayment from a present value interest-factor TABLE: 2024 Advanced uses the GP formula only

solutions.latex:
Four years of monthly payments gives $n=4\times12=48$ periods. The monthly rate is
$$r=\dfrac{4.2\%}{12}=0.35\%=0.0035$$
From the table, for $n=48$ and $r=0.0035$ the factor is $44.11376$.
$$\begin{aligned} PV &= 500\times44.11376 \\ &= \$22\,056.88 \end{aligned}$$

meta.format_note: Source gave no marks breakdown; criteria rows written by us in NESA style. Checked: 500 x 44.11376 = 22 056.88.

solutions.latex:
The future value is the present value compounded for $n=48$ periods at $r=0.0035$.
$$\begin{aligned} FV &= PV(1+r)^n \\ &= 22\,056.88\times(1+0.0035)^{48} \\ &= \$26\,084.24 \end{aligned}$$

For the loan, $PV=\$49\,000$, $n=46$ and $r=0.005$. From the table the factor is $41.00219$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Monthly repayment} &= \dfrac{49\,000}{41.00219} \\ &= \$1195.06 \\ \text{Total repaid} &= 1195.06\times46 \\ &= \$54\,972.76 \\ \text{Interest} &= 54\,972.76-49\,000 \\ &= \$5972.76 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the monthly repayment, or equivalent merit

2451.stem:
Aida has \$500 000 in an investment account earning interest at a rate of 3% per annum compounded annually.

At the end of the first year, Aida withdraws \$25 000 for expenses.

Each subsequent year, the amount that Aida withdraws increases by 5% due to rising expenses.

Let $A_n$ be the balance of Aida’s investment account at the end of the $n$th year.

parts.latex: For how many complete years will Aida be able to withdraw money from this account in order to meet her expenses?

meta.format_note: Source gave no marks breakdown; criteria rows written by us in NESA style.

solutions.latex:
Continuing the pattern of part (a), after $n$ years
$$A_n=500\,000(1.03)^n-25\,000\left[(1.05)^{n-1}+(1.05)^{n-2}(1.03)+\cdots+(1.03)^{n-1}\right]$$
The money runs out when $A_n=0$.
$$25\,000\left[(1.05)^{n-1}+(1.05)^{n-2}(1.03)+\cdots+(1.03)^{n-1}\right]=500\,000(1.03)^n$$
Divide both sides by $25\,000(1.03)^{n-1}$:
$$\left(\dfrac{1.05}{1.03}\right)^{n-1}+\cdots+\dfrac{1.05}{1.03}+1=20(1.03)=20.6$$
The left side is a geometric series with $a=1$, $r=\dfrac{1.05}{1.03}$ and $n$ terms, so
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{\left(\frac{1.05}{1.03}\right)^n-1}{\frac{1.05}{1.03}-1} &= 20.6 \\ \left(\dfrac{1.05}{1.03}\right)^n-1 &= 0.4 \\ \left(\dfrac{1.05}{1.03}\right)^n &= 1.4 \\ n &= \dfrac{\ln1.4}{\ln\left(\frac{1.05}{1.03}\right)} \\ &\approx 17.496 \end{aligned}$$
The balance is still positive after 17 withdrawals and cannot cover the 18th, so Aida can withdraw money for 17 complete years.
criteria: Forms the geometric series equation and solves for $n$, or equivalent merit
Writes $A_n=0$ with the general expression for $A_n$, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Source gave no marks breakdown; criteria rows written by us in NESA style. The step 'divide by 25 000(1.03)^(n-1)' is shown in full (the handwriting did it in two lines). The conclusion sentence was added by us; checked: A_n > 0 exactly when (1.05/1.03)^n < 1.4, true for n = 17 and false for n = 18. Source wrote 'withdraw money 17 times'.

parts.latex: What are the values of $X$ and $Y$?

The account balance, $\$A_n$, at the end of $n$ months is given by the recurrence relation

$$A_n = \left(A_{n-1} + 500\right) \times q$$

What is the value of $q$?
Find the time, to the nearest whole month, that it takes for Sienna to reach her savings goal.

solutions.latex:
Interest for the first month is the monthly rate times the balance of $\$500$.
$$X = \dfrac{4.2\%}{12}\times 500 = \$1.75$$
The balance is the previous balance, plus the deposit, plus the interest.
$$Y = 1005.26 + 500 + 5.27 = \$1510.53$$
criteria: Finds the value of $X$ or $Y$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The monthly growth factor is
$$q = 1 + \dfrac{4.2\%}{12} = 1.0035$$

Build up the balance month by month.
$$A_1 = 500\times 1.0035$$
$$\begin{aligned} A_2 &= \left(500(1.0035) + 500\right)\times 1.0035 \\ &= 500(1.0035)^2 + 500(1.0035) \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} A_3 &= \left(500(1.0035)^2 + 500(1.0035) + 500\right)\times 1.0035 \\ &= 500(1.0035)^3 + 500(1.0035)^2 + 500(1.0035) \\ &= 500(1.0035)\left(1 + 1.0035 + 1.0035^2\right) \end{aligned}$$
Continuing the pattern, the bracket is a geometric series with $a = 1$, $r = 1.0035$ and $n$ terms.
$$A_n = 500(1.0035)\left(1 + 1.0035 + 1.0035^2 + \cdots + 1.0035^{n-1}\right)$$
Set $A_n = 50\,000$ and use the sum of a GP.
$$\begin{aligned} 50\,000 &= 500(1.0035)\times\dfrac{1.0035^n - 1}{0.0035} \\ \dfrac{2707}{2007} &= 1.0035^n \\ n &= \dfrac{\log\left(\frac{2707}{2007}\right)}{\log 1.0035} \\ &\approx 85.64 \end{aligned}$$
Therefore it will take 86 months for Sienna to reach her savings goal.
criteria: Makes progress towards solution, or equivalent merit
Expresses $A_n$ in terms of a geometric progression, or equivalent merit
